prerequisites: General access requirements for the Master in Energy Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
That students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
The ability to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
The ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

The ability for autonomous learning that allows continued study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Assessment and application of advanced technologies for thermoelectric generation with minimum pollutant emissions.
Carry out the basic design of a low-temperature solar thermal installation, in accordance with the applicable legislation for this type of installation.
Identify the elements of a solar thermoelectric generation installation and apply knowledge about thermal machines to this type of installation.
Carry out the basic design of a grid-isolated photovoltaic solar installation.

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4.0 out of 10 on the written exam is required to average with the practical and seminar grades; if below 4.0, the final grade is the exam grade. If the exam score is 4.0 or higher, the exam counts for 75% and practices/seminars for 25%. The 25% for practices/seminars is divided into 10% for classroom practice presentations and 15% for laboratory/computer lab practices. For the extraordinary call, if practices and seminars were completed, the assessment is the same as the ordinary call; otherwise, a single exam covering all theoretical and practical content is given, with a minimum passing score of 5.0 out of 10. For differentiated evaluation, a final written exam covers all theoretical and practical content.
